title: Sundiata, the Epic of Mali
objective: After this level you can retell the epic of Mali's founder and explain how griots have kept it alive by performance.
summary: Sundiata Keita founded Mali in the 13th century. In the epic, the boy who could not walk stands up on an iron bar and defeats Sumanguru at Kirina. Griots, many with the kora, keep it alive.

cards.headline: Mali's founder was a boy who couldn't walk.
cards.body: Sundiata Keita, who died in 1255, founded the Mali Empire in West Africa. We know his life from oral traditions repeated by griots, West Africa's storytellers. Here's the story they tell, and then the storytellers themselves.

cards.headline: The boy who stood up
cards.body: In the epic, Sogolon's son can't walk as a child, and he and his mother are mocked at court. Then, in one great effort, he pulls himself to his feet on a huge iron bar, and the bar bends into the shape of a bow. The boy everyone laughed at is standing, and the bar isn't.

cards.headline: Exile and return
cards.body: Here the epic meets history. Sumanguru, ruler of a neighboring state, overran Sundiata's homeland and killed his brothers, sparing him because he was a sickly boy. Sundiata went into exile, then came back and defeated Sumanguru decisively at the Battle of Kirina, about 1235.

cards.headline: The griot's kora
cards.body: Griots, called jeli in the Mande languages, are hereditary troubadour-historians. They preserve genealogies, histories and oral traditions, and many play the kora, a long-necked harp lute with 21 strings. In 1960 Djibril Tamsir Niane published a French retelling of the epic, presented as told by the griot Djeli Mamadou Kouyate. Even on paper, a griot does the talking.

mascot.line: This connects to Level 6: like Homer's singers, griots carry an epic by voice, not by page.

questions.prompt: Put these moments from Sundiata's story in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Sundiata went into exile, came back to win the Battle of Kirina (about 1235) and died in 1255. Niane published a French retelling of his epic in 1960.
